title: Date navigation lists exact-date readings only

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited commit c828bc0 against the current sprint file, re-read fresh.

The status warning reports that the devteam2 sprint-31 worktree has a different copy of the sprint file. I diffed the two: the only difference is the lifecycle-owned status: line (todo there, in_progress here). There is no requirement drift. No criterion asserts anything between versions.

R1 Met. Migration 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings.sql.
- displayed_readings() is the only place the displayed-row rule is written. It filters horoscope is not null, then takes distinct on (event_date) ordered by event_date, horoscope_generated_at desc nulls last, created_at desc, id desc. Within each date, that tiebreak is exactly 20261115211107's.
- get_reading_by_date is create-or-replaced on top of it: select d.* where event_date = reading_date, limit 1, with the same signature, the same setof readings return, security definer and the same search_path. Drift is prevented by sharing the rule, not by a second copy.
- The predicate is events -> 'matchedYear' = 'true'::jsonb, written once in navigable_reading_dates(). Checked against each R1 case:
  - events null gives null, so the row is excluded.
  - A missing key gives null, so it is excluded.
  - JSON null or false is not equal to 'true'::jsonb, so it is excluded.
  - The string "true" is '"true"'::jsonb, a different jsonb value, so it is excluded.
  - Only the JSON boolean true passes.
- The filter is applied to the displayed row per date, never to any row on the date.

R2 Met.
- Both Sprint 29 functions are create-or-replaced, not dropped, so the ACL from 20261122142918 is preserved: anon and authenticated only, revoked from PUBLIC and service_role.
- Names and signatures are unchanged.
- Return types are still table (previous_date date, next_date date) and table (event_date date).
- Both are still security definer with a pinned search_path.
- Adjacency is strict < and > over the qualifying set, so a non-qualifying date is skipped over.
- The recent list orders by the displayed row's horoscope_generated_at desc nulls last, then event_date desc. limit 20 applies after the filter.
- Both helpers have execute revoked from public, anon, authenticated and service_role. Neither is security definer. Callers reach them through the owner rights of the security definer functions.
- The migration ends with its schema_migrations insert.

R3 and R4 Met. There is no diff under app/ or lib/ between 3568b56 and c828bc0; the only other commit in between is CLAUDE.md. The page lookup's row selection is semantically identical.

R5 Met. reading-date-navigation-exact-year.test.ts covers:
- matchedYear true is listed and is a neighbour on both sides;
- false, null events, a missing key and the string "true" are each excluded and skipped, plus JSON null as an extra case;
- both subtlety cases, named as such, each also asserting what get_reading_by_date shows;
- the R3 case: a non-qualifying page still returns its reading;
- the cap: 22 qualifying casts interleaved with newer non-qualifying ones, expecting exactly the last 20 qualifying dates, newest first, which proves the cap applies after the filter;
- adjacency skipping three different non-qualifying dates, including from inside the gap;
- anon rpc to both helpers erroring.
The Sprint 29 suite changed in seed data only: an EXACT_YEAR_EVENTS payload in insertReading and in the nulls-last fixture insert. No assertion changed.

Ran these myself:
- npm test: 25 files, 260 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean, /date/[date] dynamic.
I could NOT run test:rls: no docker in this WSL distro. CI's rls-tests job is its first real run, and Pipeman's push report must show it green.

Low, non-blocking:
(a) displayed_readings has a SET search_path clause, so Postgres won't inline it. get_reading_by_date now does a distinct-on over every horoscope row on each page view, and get_adjacent_reading_dates evaluates the helper twice. This is fine at this table size, the cost the sprint file's own Risks accept. Revisit with an index or rewrite if readings grow.
(b) Same shape as Sprint 29's note (a): the clusters are random 5-day spans in 2200-2790, about 12 per run. Within one run, the chance two collide is roughly 0.3%. It grows on a persistent local database. Not blocking, but a CI flake there is this, not a defect.

No new Human Prerequisites beyond the sprint file's. No test was labelled known-failing.
commit=c828bc0 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for c828bc01277fcfc42168fe4cf1bf080db90b46ed all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested on 2026-11-22 against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit c828bc0. Production serves the pushed bookkeeping tip ac87051: /api/health/db
reports status ok, migrationVersion 20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings, commit
ac87051. git diff --stat c828bc0 ac87051 touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-30.json.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57, real link clicks), curl against Supabase REST with
the anon/publishable key the user supplied in Sprint 29, and gh run view --log.

CI: runs 45039369504 (c828bc0) and 45039825722 (ac87051). build, rls-tests and migrate all
succeed in both.
- rls-tests: 43 passed, including reading-date-navigation-exact-year.test.ts with 13 tests.
- Unit tests: 260 passed.
- migrate: applied 20261122152710 in the first run and printed "Remote database is up to
  date." in the second. "No drift detected." in both.

STEP 1, find non-qualifying dates: PASS. No cast was needed. I called rpc get_reading_by_date
with the anon key for all 33 dates from Sprint 29's full prev/next walk, plus 2050-06-15.
- 10 of 33 qualify, meaning the displayed reading's events.matchedYear is true: 1776-07-04,
  1920-08-18, 1945-05-08, 1963-11-22, 1969-07-20, 1976-07-04, 1977-08-16, 1986-03-31,
  1991-06-12 and 2001-09-11.
- 23 are false, for example 1900-01-01, 1969-07-21, 1984-02-29, 2026-12-16, 2050-06-15 and
  2100-12-31. None had events null.
- A date I did not cast appeared since Sprint 29: 1929-10-24, created 2026-11-22T15:33:09Z,
  matchedYear true. That makes 11 qualifying dates in production.
- LiveQA cast nothing this sprint. The 2050-06-15 reading is the one I cast in Sprint 29.

STEP 2, non-qualifying dates absent and skipped: PASS.
- The recent list on every page I checked holds exactly the 11 qualifying dates, in this
  order: 1929-10-24, 1991-06-12, 2001-09-11, 1969-07-20, 1977-08-16, 1976-07-04, 1920-08-18,
  1776-07-04, 1945-05-08, 1963-11-22, 1986-03-31. That matches each displayed reading's
  horoscope_generated_at, newest first.
- None of the 23 non-qualifying dates appear.
- Skipping:
  - 1776-07-04 next is 1920-08-18, skipping 1900-01-01.
  - 1969-07-20 neighbours skip 1969-07-21, 1969-07-23, 1977-03-31 and 1984-02-29; for
    example 1984-02-29's page shows prev 1977-08-16 and next 1986-03-31.
  - 2001-09-11 has next null, skipping every 2008 to 2100 date.
- The non-qualifying pages still render in full, HTTP 200 with the horoscope WRITTEN, and
  "What happened" reads "ON THIS DAY, OTHER YEARS". This held for /date/1900-01-01,
  /date/1969-07-21, /date/1984-02-29 and /date/2050-06-15.
- On those pages there is no aria-current entry in the recent list. That is correct, because
  they aren't in it.

STEP 3, every linked date is exact-date: PASS. I clicked each of the 11 distinct linked dates
(the union of prev, next and the recent list across 9 pages) from /date/1900-01-01. All 11
landed on a WRITTEN page whose "What happened" reads "THIS EXACT DATE <year>":
1776, 1920, 1929, 1945, 1963, 1969-07-20, 1976, 1977, 1986, 1991 and 2001.
On qualifying pages the current date is a SPAN with aria-current, not a link. This held for
1776-07-04, 1929-10-24, 1991-06-12 and 2001-09-11.

STEP 4, dates only via anon: PASS.
- get_recent_reading_dates returned HTTP 200: 11 objects, each only {"event_date":...}.
- get_adjacent_reading_dates returned only previous_date and next_date:
  - 1900-01-01 gave 1776-07-04 and 1920-08-18.
  - 1776-07-04 gave null and 1920-08-18.
  - 2001-09-11 gave 1991-06-12 and null.
  - 1969-07-21 gave 1969-07-20 and 1976-07-04.
- The new helpers are closed to anon:
  - POST rpc/displayed_readings returned HTTP 401, code 42501, "permission denied for
    function displayed_readings". GET returned the same.
  - POST rpc/navigable_reading_dates returned HTTP 401, code 42501, "permission denied for
    function navigable_reading_dates".
- An anon select on readings still returns HTTP 200 with [].

STEP 5, 390px: PASS. I used isMobile at 390x844 on /date/1900-01-01, 1776-07-04, 2001-09-11
and 1929-10-24. scrollWidth is 390 both with "RECENTLY WRITTEN (11)" closed and with it open.
With it open there are 11 items and no element extends past 390px.

No console or page errors.
Observation, not a defect: with 11 of 34 dates qualifying, the list currently holds 11, not
20. The sprint's Risks section accepts that.
